knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Pond water, sludge and fish are not released without a confirmed route with the council and water authority. The route must be checked before any move.
A bucket test separates evaporation from a leak. Topping up without the cause makes the loss worse and hides a fault.
In NSW, releasing fish into public waters needs a fish stocking permit, and dumping an unwanted fish is an offence. The technician refuses and records the request.

practicalCriteria: Learner sets up a simulated bucket test, marks the levels correctly and states what a result of greater loss outside the bucket means
Learner declines a planted request to drain a pond to a kerb drain and records the confirmed-route requirement and the referral
Learner records a simulated top-up with volume, reason, approval and the person who approved it
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark. With three questions, all three must be correct. Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation and is not verified by this quiz.
evidenceRequired: Bucket test record with levels, weather and result
Referral note for a refused discharge request, with the route check recorded
Water-movement record showing volume, route, approval and approving person
Assessor observation of the bucket test set-up
stopWorkCriteria: No approved discharge route is confirmed for the water, sludge or plants
A fish is to be released, moved or sold without the state permit or rule that applies
Unexplained rapid water loss that suggests a leak in a pond with live fish
